content:
When searching mathlib statement names, leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib_docs (mathlib3) consistently outranks the mathlib4 docs. I tested this across Google and DuckDuckGo and I don't think it's a personalization issue (but I would appreciate if others could verify this). As a concrete example, Icc_eq_filter_powerset lists leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib_docs first and leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs second. In particular for people new to Lean having a fully (?) deprecated version listed first could be confusing.

Maybe someone with more SEO experience can chime in, but I think the usual approach would be adding a <link rel="canonical" href="[mathlib4-equivalent]"> to mathlib3 declaration pages? This keeps mathlib3 accessible but suggests search engines to go to the mathlib4 version instead and should consolidate link equity, i.e., it should boost mathlib4's ranking without de-listing anything or losing acquired "search engine capital". The main challenge would probably be constructing the URL mapping between the two. Notably there is already a self-referential <link rel="canonical" href="https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib_docs/data/finset/interval.html"> in the header, so the infrastructure is in place — the fix would be updating the canonical_roots mapping in `print_docs.py in leanprover-community/doc-gen to point to mathlib4 equivalents instead.

Has anyone looked into this? Is the URL mapping tractable? I'd be up for giving this a shot and drafting a PR to doc-gen.py if this idea hasn't already been floated and dismissed (couldn't find any prior discussion on Zulip). Though the fact that the repo is archived probably means this might need some workarounds or ad hoc fixes to the actually deployed pages rather than a PR.
I don't understand why the mathlib3 docs are still up at all. People who need them can build them locally. After all, that's what one must do in order to read even just last week's mathlib docs.
Because links from papers point to them

Snir Broshi said:

Because links from papers point to them

Can one fix a version or commit to point to the docs at a specific state? And if so, have most papers bothered to do so in the past? Without that I would expect a significant chunk of references to be broken anyways, unless there is some clever fallback resolution in place?

Either way, canonical links (to my understanding) should not impact direct visitors but resolve the search engine issue. Though possibly the "search engine capital" is not that relevant if mathlib4 is already at second place. A simpler solution might be to just "de-list" the mathlib3 docs from search engines but keeping the URLs alive for direct visitors.

Snir Broshi said:

Because links from papers point to them

Fortunately the internet archive has thoroughly archived the entirety of lean 3 docs so people should still be able to find it https://web.archive.org/web/20250818061717/https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib_docs/data/finset/interval.html

So a rough test seems to suggest that a naive snake_case to CamelCase matching covers about 67.1% of files, using the port status yaml covers about 77.4%, following the git re-name chain in mathlib4 on top of that gets us to 92.3%. The rest one could just point to mathlib4 documentation root. The question is whether this would be fine as a one-off update of the final deployed mathlib3 docs that covers (currently) 77.4%, or if it should be continuously updated with git re-name changes for maybe a year to get to 90%+ until all search engines have updated their index.

Of course, this ignores if the contents of a file migrated with the original file remaining. I think there was some Basic.leanto Defs.leanchurn? Don't think there is much that can be done about that and it is probably irrelevant for the search engine indexing question.
Some files have also been split, or lemmas have been moved. There is no perfect one-to-one matching of files, especially over time.

Michael Rothgang said:

Some files have also been split, or lemmas have been moved. There is no perfect one-to-one matching of files, especially over time.

Yes, but the canonical link would (afaik) not point users to the new page based on a concrete search result, but just tell a search engine "there is a newer authoritative version of this page, please attribute accordingly", so it accounts for the new content but allows mathlib4 to inherit the earned ranking of mathlib3.

Of course that newer version might not cover the actual contents that someone might have linked to the mathlib3 version for, but this was already an issue before and is still an issue now in mathlib4: whenever things move and someone just linked to a generic docs page and the contents change or move, the link is effectively broken. mathlib docs seem continuously updated and have no commit or version history, so that is inherent to that design.

But the discussion about moved statements or split files is largely orthogonal for what I am suggesting / bothered by: I merely would want mathlib3 to no longer appear at the top of the search indices.

  1. We can wait another year or two until mathlib4 naturally overtakes it for the majority of searches (accepting that some stragglers may survive much longer than that).
  2. We can hard de-index mathlib3 since mathlib4 docs already seem to rank second.
  3. Or we can try to migrate some search capital from mathlib3 to mathlib4 with canonical links. Even a blanket pointer to the mathlib4 doc main page would probably achieve that.

Snir Broshi said:

Because links from papers point to them

But some links from papers to the mathlib4 docs are broken all the time. If you really want your paper to link to something in mathlib, it is your responsability to point to a frozen version you are managing yourself.
Exactly, the mathlib3 docs are frozen :sweat_smile:
Yes, but my point is that only the papers that were written about the very last version of mathlib3 stand a chance to correctly point to the docs. I assume this is a very small minority of papers
Those doc pages were never versioned. Are there any paper actually linking to that? I would be pretty surprised. I think papers link to GitHub, including a commit sha or a specific branch or tag.

I find the mathlib3 docs quite valuable for doing a git blame back into the mathlib3 days:

  • Do a git blame in mathlib4
  • jump back until you see an align
  • look up the declaration in the mathlib3_docs to jump to the right place on github to continue

Christoph Spiegel said:

Notably there is already a self-referential <link rel="canonical" href="https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib_docs/data/finset/interval.html"> in the header

Note the purpose of this was to avoid google indexing copies of the docs hosted for university courses.

Eric Wieser said:

I find the mathlib3 docs quite valuable for doing a git blame back into the mathlib3 days:

  • Do a git blame in mathlib4
  • jump back until you see an align
  • look up the declaration in the mathlib3_docs to jump to the right place on github to continue

You could still do that after moving those docs to some place which is less visible to search engines, right?
Yes, that was only an argument to hedge against any "Let's delete them entirely" proposal

I won't be able to put together any changes personally in the next few weeks, but I'd be happy to unarchive https://github.com/leanprover-community/doc-gen and review PRs if there's consensus on what we should do.
Why do you need docs for git blame? git grep on a local checkout of mathlib3 works just fine.

Bryan Gin-ge Chen said:

I won't be able to put together any changes personally in the next few weeks, but I'd be happy to unarchive https://github.com/leanprover-community/doc-gen and review PRs if there's consensus on what we should do.

I'd be happy to draft a PR with the canonical link change.

Though I just did some more research and it looks like the consensus on whether canonical links are the right tool here (or will even be respected by search engines) is mixed... it is a apparently a reasonably standard SEO practice but at the same time Google might ignore it if it deems the content between pages "too different". Bing just straight up prefers a 301. So really, besides waiting, that would just leave a <meta name="robots" content="noindex">: the mathlib3 docs stay online and links still work, but they simply do not show up in search results.

I've unarchived the repo. In addition to any meta tag changes, we should also add a banner to the page template letting visitors know that the whole site is outdated and pointing them to the lean4 docs.
https://github.com/leanprover-community/doc-gen/pull/180 adds a banner

I suggested some CSS changes to the banner formatting. On the canonical link I think just pointing to the root of mathlib4 docs is going to get it ignored by Google for sure. So either we give an updated mathlib3 to mathlib4 map a try (admittedly derived with this vibe coded script) or we just de-index.

I've merged the CSS scripts.

I agree that even an approximate map is probably good enough, there's very little additional value in marginal improvements to the map...

I'm not entirely sure where the map should live / how it should be hooked up. @Christoph Spiegel, do you have a definitive idea?
Ideally we can get a few +1s on the idea of just committing a best-quick-effort map as a once-off? And then we'll merge whatever Christoph has in mind? :-)
+1 to the general idea
Sounds fine, but why not "de-index", or even just map every page to the root of the mathlib4 docs? Does making a map help search engines somehow?

Kim Morrison said:

I'm not entirely sure where the map should live / how it should be hooked up. Christoph Spiegel, do you have a definitive idea?

Not really. The base was leanprover-community/mathlib3/wiki/mathlib4-port-status-yaml that covered around 77%, with git mv tracking to bump it to 94%. Since that wiki is presumably also frozen, probably the simplest solution is to just commit it to root of leanprover-community/doc-gen? That directory doesn't seem the tidiest anyways, so one more file won't hurt :smile:

Alternatives are to just use the 77% version (requires a bit more python code work) and avoid committing another map or to simply de-index.

Snir Broshi said:

Sounds fine, but why not "de-index", or even just map every page to the root of the mathlib4 docs? Does making a map help search engines somehow?

You can just "get rid of" mathlib3 in the results with a de-index but that also loses its acquired "search capital". Since mathlib4 is already pretty high in the search rankings, that is still a perfectly valid approach in my opinion.

The original reason behind suggesting the canonical link was that it in theory allows you to not completely lose the page index ranking that mathlib3 has acquired over the years and try to transfer it to mathlib4. The caveat is that "canonical links" are intended for pages that are essentially identical in content. Whether or not they are actually respected by the search engines and what their idea of "essentially identical" is seems to be a bit of a rabbit hole... at least that is what a bit of Googling and asking Claude indicated to me when I tried to understand this better. The "essentially identical in content" is btw is also why just pointing to mathlib4 root quite likely is not a good idea. Best case it just behaves like a no-index, worst case it is completely ignored.

But I could find at least one specific example of using canonical links for stale docs: Django links to 6.0 from as far back as 1.11 and it seems to work :man_shrugging: Python2 to 3 afaik handled this more poorly with a disallow: /2/ in docs.python.org/robots.txt that wasn't really respected by Google.
Relevant links: Read the Docs on canonical URLs for exactly this use case, the Django discussion, and the Python discussion
Relatedly, I think we should _not_ change the canonical link for the homepage, to allow people who really want the mathlib 3 docs to be able to find them.
(but indeed we want to drive search away from every other subpage)

How does the canonical link prevent people from finding the docs?
FWIW I just searched "python 2 docs" on Google and the first result contained a canonical link which is different than itself. So it doesn't look like google cares much about canonical links anyway.
The canonical link still goes to a page about python 2 though

It took a few weeks but I finally merged leanprover-community/doc-gen#180 (and the added mathlib3 to mathlib4 map in leanprover-community/doc-gen#181). Thanks to @Christoph Spiegel and @Kim Morrison for their PRs!

Please check out https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib_docs/ and let me know if there's anything else urgent we should fix before I archive the repo again.

Thank you all! Question: can we make the banner link to the mapped URL when there is one? It could 404 if the mathlib4 file moves (since we won't be maintaining the map), but I think it'll be useful as long as mathlib3 wins SEO. (we could also later fix docgen4's 404 page to have a link to the root)
Also not sure if it's intentional but pages that aren't in the map have their canonical link set to the old docs, e.g. https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib_docs/combinatorics/simple_graph/connectivity.html
I would be happy to review / merge a PR addressing those but I probably won't have time to work on those myself!
